Consult Summary:
- Adult patient with 2-day history of gradually worsening, constant lower abdominal pain (below umbilicus) with subjective fever/sweats, mild nausea, and pink-tinged urine; empirically treated for presumed urinary tract infection (UTI) and advised pregnancy test and safety-net follow-up.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Lower abdominal pain below the belly button; burning quality; constant; gradually worsening over 2 days; localized (no radiation). Able to function/walk but aware of pain.
- Associated symptoms: Felt hot/sweaty (no measured temperature), mild nausea (no vomiting), reported increased urination (also increased fluid intake), pink-tinged urine; no dysuria; prior constipation last week now resolved; no diarrhea.
- Pertinent negatives: No shortness of breath, cough, palpitations, headaches, or vision changes.
- Gynecologic/sexual history: Sexually active with same partner; last intercourse 4 days ago. On contraceptive implant (Implanon) inserted ~1 year ago. Still having periods. Last menstrual period reported as “about three weeks ago… I mean two weeks ago” (conflict noted). Prior STI screen 6 months ago normal. Pregnancy possible but not suspected by patient.
- Past medical/surgical history: No prior similar episodes. No surgical history reported. No chronic conditions reported.
- Medications: Contraceptive implant (Implanon). No other regular medications reported.
- Allergies: Not discussed.
- Family history: No relevant family history (including bowel-related) reported.
- Social history: Lives in a shared house with two roommates. Works as an accountant. Non-smoker. Drinks alcohol socially.

Impression:
- Working diagnosis: Suspected urinary tract infection. Differential discussed: gastrointestinal cause vs pregnancy-related cause also considered.

Plan:
- Empiric antibiotics: Trimethoprim tablets—1 tablet twice daily for 3 days; route and tablet strength not documented. Prescription sent to patient’s pharmacy; start today.
- Symptomatic care: Paracetamol for pain; maintain good oral hydration; cranberry juice may help urinary symptoms.
- Testing: Pregnancy test advised to exclude pregnancy.
- Follow-up/safety net: Return in a few days if no improvement, or sooner for red flags (worsening abdominal pain, persistent fever/hot/sweaty, vomiting). Investigations were discussed initially; patient opted to trial empiric treatment first, with plan to reassess if not improving.

Quality checks:
● Missing expected elements: Allergies; vitals; physical exam; urinalysis/culture not performed; pregnancy test not yet done; medication strength and route for trimethoprim not documented.  
● Internal conflicts: Patient name addressed as “Tim” initially and “Kim” later (conflict noted). Last menstrual period stated as both ~3 weeks and ~2 weeks ago (conflict noted).  
● Transcript quality: Generally clear; occasional hesitations/overlaps but clinically interpretable.
